text: I feel nervous about tomorrow, even though I prepared well.
I attended classes and came home at five.
I miss her, but I am grateful for the time we shared.
I trust my friend to support me when things get difficult.
I am eagerly looking forward to our trip tomorrow.
Their cruel behaviour disgusted me.
I am not happy with how today went.

Third time this week my project partner has uploaded his section at midnight without telling anyone, and then he acts like I'm being dramatic for asking about it. I spent my whole evening fixing his formatting again. Honestly I'm tired of covering for him and I'm done pretending it doesn't bother me.

The landlord said he'd fix the leaking tap last month, then again two weeks ago, and again yesterday. Now he's texting me that I should have reminded him nicely. I read that message four times with my jaw clenched, typing and deleting replies until I finally put my phone face down.

My cousin borrowed my camera for the family trip and returned it with a cracked lens, shrugging like it was nothing. He didn't even say sorry, he just asked if I could send him the photos. I'm not going to reply tonight because I know I'll say something I can't take back.

Mum slipped my favourite mango pickle into my bag again before I left for the hostel, wrapped in three layers of plastic so it wouldn't leak. I found it while unpacking and stood there holding the jar, feeling so looked after that I almost called her right then.

We've been together two years, and I used to think he barely noticed what I said. Today he handed me a second-hand copy of the out-of-print novel I'd mentioned once, months ago, with a sticky note saying only found it. I keep running my thumb over the cover because it feels like proof that he really listens to me.

Sat with Nana on the balcony this evening while she told me the same story about her village for the fifth time. I didn't mind at all, and I could have listened all night. Her hand on my shoulder and the smell of her talcum powder made me want to stay close to her for as long as I can.

I walked into the lab expecting a normal Tuesday and found the whole batch of samples already processed, with a note saying the professor had come in at six. Nobody had told us the equipment would be back so early. I read the note twice because I assumed I'd walked into the wrong room.

Was scrolling past the department notice board when I saw my own name on the scholarship list. I hadn't even been sure my form went through properly. For a full minute I just stared, convinced it was a typo, and then I checked my roll number twice.

At the station I opened my bag and found a rubber duck, half a packet of chips and absolutely no laptop. It took a minute to realise I'd grabbed my little brother's identical bag from the hallway. I stood frozen on the platform, mouth open, while the train I needed pulled away.

I handed Meera my laptop with the whole thesis draft on it and went to catch my bus without a second thought. She's backed up my files before and has never once lost anything. Knowing she'd handle it properly meant I could actually relax on the ride home.

When the new tutor said he'd review my report by Friday, I believed him right away. Last semester I'd have checked in every day because my old supervisor kept forgetting, but this time I'm not worried at all. He's done exactly what he said he would every single time so far.

The trek to Kasol is only nine days away and I've already laid my backpack out on the floor. Every evening I check the weather forecast and rewatch the route videos, counting down the days. I can't wait to finally be standing in those mountains.

My sister lands from Pune on Friday, and I've been planning the whole weekend in my head for days. We'll hit the old chaat stall first, then rewatch our favourite movies until late. I keep glancing at the calendar, wishing Friday would hurry up.

Opened the shared fridge in the hostel to find someone's leftover curry had grown a fuzzy green coat, sitting right next to my curd. The smell hit me before I even saw it. I gagged, shut the door fast and washed my hands three times afterwards.

At the canteen today I watched the cook scratch his arm and then go straight back to kneading dough with the same bare hands. I'm not usually squeamish about food, but my stomach turned over and I pushed my plate away untouched. I think I'll be eating outside the campus for a while.

Took the metro to the library around eleven and returned two books that were due on the twelfth. Then I picked up a printout of the syllabus and sat in the reading hall for about an hour. Left by one to catch the bus home.

Finished the lab report by mid-afternoon and sent it to the group for comments. After that I ironed two shirts, reheated rice for dinner and checked tomorrow's timetable. The first lecture starts at 9:15 in room 204.

Said goodbye to the old flat today after the movers took the last box, and my chest felt heavy walking through the empty rooms one more time. But then my sister called to say the keys to our new place were ready, and I laughed out loud for the first time all week. It's strange to feel both of those in the same hour.

I leave for my exchange semester in Berlin in six days, and every time I picture the airport alone my palms go cold. I keep imagining losing my passport or getting on the wrong train. But I've also saved a list of bookshops I'm desperate to see, and I smile every time I scroll through it.

My brother cancelled my birthday dinner at the last minute for a cricket match, and I was so irritated I hung up on him. Later he turned up at my door with a cake and a clumsy apology, and I still felt annoyed even as I hugged him tightly. I'm not letting this go quickly, but I'm also glad he's my brother.
